data.name: Sajith
data.gender_notes: Sajith is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sajith is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Sageetha' which means 'Sage, Seer, Wise'. This name is often given to children who are believed to have a deep understanding of the world and a strong sense of intuition. The name Sajith carries the meaning “Sage, Seer, Wise” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil, Malayalam. Parents who choose Sajith usually hope their child will grow to embody sage, seer, wise and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sajith is a divine name associated with the Hindu god Vishnu. It is believed that those named Sajith are blessed with the wisdom and knowledge of the universe, and have the ability to see beyond the physical world.
data.etymology: Sajith belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sage, Seer, Wise.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sajith total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

In Hindu mythology, sages and seers are revered figures, known for their knowledge, wisdom, and connection to the divine. The name Sajith honors this tradition, and can inspire a child to strive for intellectual and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Sajith is believed to bestow the qualities of wisdom, insight, and intuition upon the bearer. It is a reminder that true knowledge comes not only from external sources, but also from within oneself. The name also encourages the pursuit of enlightenment and self-realization, helping the individual to deepen their connection to the divine and live a meaningful and purposeful life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sajith, meaning victorious or successful, is a name often given in Hindu culture to acknowledge the divine presence of Lord Vishnu in one's life, symbolizing the individual's potential for overcoming challenges and achieving success.
